description: The foundation of Ty Mawr near St Dochdwy's Church. Built on the remains of a significant Celtic monastery.
narration: Our story begins in 1215. Ty Mawr, the Great House, is established on ground that had already seen centuries of sacred use. It stands as a sentinel of Welsh history, unaware that its ownership would one day spark a 33-year legal war.

scenes.text: This land is sacred. It has seen fifteen centuries of silence and prayer.
We build for eternity. These walls are thicker than a man is tall.

description: The modern dispute begins. Differences over land boundaries and access rights emerge between neighbors.
narration: Fast forward nearly eight centuries. The year is 1991. What began as a minor disagreement over a strip of land at Great House Farm escalates. The long peace is broken, and the lawyers are called in.

scenes.text: This track has always belonged to the farm. I have the deeds to prove it!
Your deeds are ancient history. The modern boundary clearly excludes this area.

description: The case reaches the High Court after years of localized legal skirmishes.
narration: By 2005, the battle moves to the high court. Hundreds of thousands of pounds have already been spent. The judges must sift through medieval deeds and modern land registry maps to find the truth.

scenes.text: The court must weigh the evidence of user-rights against the formal title.
My client has maintained this property in good faith for decades.

description: The '33-Year Odyssey' concludes. One of the longest-running land disputes in UK history.
narration: Finally, in 2024, the legal odyssey of Great House Farm reaches its conclusion. Thirty-three years of litigation, millions in costs, all for a piece of ground. A sobering reminder of the weight of history.

scenes.text: Three decades of paperwork, finally filed away.
The Great House still stands. The people pass, but the land remains.
